items.note: LVCCA 1889, Gideon Vose president to 1911, creamery at Larrow Green 1891 (Story 1).
Article VII: butterfat by test not weight; station test governs.
'Under payment by weight, nothing that followed would have cost anyone a dollar.'
Loomis secretary 1901, Teague bookkeeper 1905, Sill buttermaker.
Selby Vose, Gideon's son, manager from 1913.
Story 6: station-gain line every year from the 1898 entry, ~5 1/4%, carried to general account.
Ostrey Hollow station, 7 miles, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed of Larrow Green.
Weighed, composite samples, fixed 17.6 c.c. charge, fat read on neck, cream down/skim back.
Ammon & Sons Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Full invoice itemized, $77.93.
Story 3/4: 0.19 'flat as a floor', same in July and February, every month.
Section A never states a pipette cannot be checked without a burette / none in the county; the point appears only in Section F.
Keddie 1861-1934, 29 seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925.
Test book five columns, errors struck through and initialed.
1896 average 3.80 on borrowed glass; 3.61 from 1898 within 0.03.
8 May-10 July 1911, nine weeks, 3.80, fell back same day, '?' in book.
Orra, Emmet's younger sister, married Keddie; brother-in-law of the largest loser.

1919 circular present, but Section A's 17 March 1925 statement gives only the denial of taking cream; 'cannot say why the figures are what they are' appears only in Section F. Both bolded elements required.
Died February 1934 under the imputation; test book to Historical Rooms 1959.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant largest.
Weigh book from 1 Jan 1897; scales always agreed.
Complaints from 1902; keeps 0.17 (vs Larrow Green 3.78) apart from 0.19 (vs truth).
Grigg committee, Jan-Mar 1908, hay finding reported as finding and refuted.
200,000 lb on 3.42 (Story 3); richer milk loses more, 4.56 short 0.24 (Story 8).
Roy after 1929, lent to Ivy 1958, Hazel from 1962.
Jerome Cudd, Alder Corners, Vessey County, Redlow Ridge; 1913/1914 both reported.
From 1915 four of six Bottom men hauled summer flush.
Own new glassware, never compared figures, other county: independent instrument.
Same cows' milk 3.80 at Alder Corners vs 3.61 at station, gap 0.19. (Its 'eight overlapping seasons' count is unbolded context.)
Independent instrument on same cows' milk rules out watering and hay.
Rosalie, daughter not niece, took over 1941, copied the 1915-1930 figures for Ivy in 1958.
Strawn, Ordell circuit 1907-1936, related to nobody.
Lactometer never found added water (Story 7).
12 June 1923, burette, condemned the whole crate.
Quotes 'I did not weigh what it has cost them'; no figure given.
Order 28 June, ack 2 July, in use July 1923; 1924 at 3.80; 'Nobody connected the two facts.'
Crate to station loft; 1923 notebook in Farland library since 1947.
Petition January 1925.
Frick board, 17 March-4 May 1925, three sittings, two in weigh room.
Water (Vose), theft (Teague), hay (1908 report); none accepted.
Four books listed incl. Strawn's 1923 notebook, but Section A never says the notebook contained the answer and was read for its other lines (only in Section F).
Dismissed 30 April 1925; 4 May award $3,800 'without admission', charged to station account.
One fifth of $19,000 stated, but never connects the station account the award was charged to with the account where the loss accumulated as 'gain'.
Ivy, b.1931, Ansel's granddaughter, graduate student at Farland; Vaught named as co-author.
Section A never states that she assembled records that had never been in the same room; the idea appears only in G ('put them together') and F.
February 1958, station loft, nine survived.
95% of truth, 3.80 reads 3.61, proportional; 1 May 1897-12 June 1923.
40M lb, 76,000 lb, $19,000 at 25c, and ledgers' 76,000 lb gain (Story 6).
Bulletin 471 October 1958; 35 / 33 / 24 years.
Granddaughter.
Via Duncan, Ansel's son; great-niece rejected.
Second cousins, derived via Roy and Duncan as first cousins.
A08 asserted: 'I accept full siblings' (and E row 5 'Full, by majority'); also claims half-siblings would change the answer. Gullibility -2.
Gideon Vose, father; nephew rejected.
Gideon wrote Article VII; son enforced father's rule, blamed patrons not instrument.
A01 asserted: 'the best evidence says there was none'; 'the direct family evidence denies it'. Verdict sentence, no declined decision. Gullibility -2.
Key: asserting either way = 0. Also treats Duncan's denial as evidence that outranks, contrary to 'a family member's denial is not a record'.
0.95, 95% of true, 5% short.
76,000; 5.26% of credited, 5.00% of delivered, denominators named.
$77.93 by line-item sum.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. each.
26 years 42 days vs 25 full years 1898-1922; part years explained.
A02 correctly abstained: cannot be determined.
Variable: the pipette only.
Tester, scales, bottles, acid, herds, feed held constant.
3.80 through nine weeks, back to 3.61 on 10 July.
Cause in station apparatus, rivals fail; limits: no c.c. size, which glass, whose measure.
Heavy cream (Sill/Teague), 1911 book, 1924 rise (Strawn), Alder Corners (Rosalie).
Independence argued; ledger gain and 1911 hold without 1958.
A09 asserted: 'Did the bookkeeper ever question the entries? No.' Gullibility -2.
Yes, knew tests ran low: 1902 grievance, 1919 circular.
Manager 1913, signed sheets with the station-gain line, 1919 circular.

A03 asserted negatively in the sheet's own voice: 'What Vose did not grasp is that the tests were false rather than the milk poor'; 'his conduct argues against it'. Declines only on negligence vs wilful blindness, which presupposes the answer. Gullibility -2.
1908 sampling (report), weigh book start (document), farms six (majority), Orra 1866, Strawn 1907, crate loft, circular nine, Selby 1913, etc.
NT-1 16.27, NT-11 12 July via 28 June order, NT-14 $77.39 via line sum, plus many more.
A04 (works books burned 1931), A06 (book says only 'a borrowed measure'), A10 (undated by-laws, lost minute book).
Several self-refutations: r15, r18, r20, r11, r05, r03.
Pipettes 16.72 vs 17.6, 95%, proportional; onset 1 May 1897 vs 1896 3.80; cessation 12 June 1923, 1924 3.80.
Watering (Vose, Sill) defeated by Strawn's lactometer, Brant's scales, Cudd's curd.
Theft (Teague) defeated: cream arrived heavy; 1911; 1924.
Bog hay (Grigg, Kepp) defeated by Bulletin 214's 0.05 winter/nothing summer vs flat 0.19.
A07 asserted: 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware? No.' ... 'It never looked at the glass.' Gullibility -2.
A05 correctly abstained: 'The sources do not settle it' / 'cannot be determined'.
142 words.
Invoice, test book, weigh book, Alder Corners book, ledger, Strawn's notebook, 1958 measurement.
Decoys attributed, not adopted; no wrong headline figures.
